top_signals.title: Oil Prices Steady as Hormuz Tanker Threats Offset Supply Glut Fears
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices steadied today after a decline earlier this week, as the perception of a return to oversupply and continued attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz basically canceled each other out. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $92.01 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $83.00 per barrel, as forecasters warn of a glut even though tanker tracking data shows flows out of the Persian Gulf are still below pre-war levels, despite the significant improvement from the early months of the war. Meanwhile, risks remain high.…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.
